name: Drawn Out (working name)
promise: What would actually happen if…? Real science, worked out and drawn by hand on one sheet of paper while you watch: sourced answers, deadpan jokes in the margins.
audience: Curious adults and teens 16-40 who like science thought experiments (xkcd What If, Kurzgesagt) but scroll Shorts; global English.

benchmarks.study: 51.4k subscribers, 8.57M views, 139 videos (channel page, 7 Oct 2026). Vertical 2-3 min 'X explained' stories drawn densely on one white page: fine-liner sketches, red and blue pencil fills, charts and hand lettering, the camera moving across the page. Median not measured yet (shorts_median 0 = unknown). We borrow the format, not the drawings: our pages are drawn in code.

voice.name: Felix (Fish Audio library, Australian male)
voice.notes: Pilot uses the studio's current voice, Kokoro George (bm_george), as the other channels do while there is no Fish key.

look.texture: one sheet of off-white drawing paper on a wooden desk; graphite-ink line work that wobbles like a hand; red and blue coloured-pencil hatching; hand lettering

captions.style: Patrick Hand, 2-5 words per chunk, ink on a white paper outline, numbers in red

safe_zone.note: px at 1080x1920; keep text out of the platform UI (title, buttons, progress bar)

look.notes: Everything is drawn in code (studio/engine/kits/sketch.js): strokes are seeded polylines revealed over time, the hand and pencil are drawn shapes that follow the stroke tip. No image model draws anything, and no text is ever generated as an image. Real people are named, never drawn.
look.direction: 'What would actually happen if…' (user 2026-10-07, after the niche research). Each beat drawn into its own part of one page; the camera pans; the last beat pulls back to the whole page. Hand: a photoreal hand cut-out is being tested (user rejected the drawn and cartoon hands).

cast.traits: plain words, dry asides, never shouts

series.name: What would actually happen if…
beats: hook: the hypothetical in one line, drawn as the first sketch
the setup: the real numbers that matter (size, speed, temperature), drawn as a diagram
the escalation: step by step, what physics or biology does next
the twist: the surprising real answer, sourced
callback: the pull-back reveals the whole page
example_titles: What would actually happen if you jumped into a hole through the Earth?
What would actually happen if the Moon disappeared?

series.name: Stories around us (occasional)
example_titles: Why your power bill went up (it's a building you've never seen)

script.tone: Calm, plain storyteller with dry asides. Explains like a friend drawing on a napkin.
rules: One idea per line. Short sentences. Deadpan: state absurd facts plainly and let the gap carry the joke.
Line one is the hook: the most surprising true sentence in the episode, under the word limit, no preamble.
Spell numbers the way they are spoken ('nineteen thirty-two', 'ten thousand'). Put the digits in the captions.
Every line with a fact, number, name or date cites dossier claim ids. Jokes may not smuggle in new facts.
Estimates and self-reported numbers carry their label on screen (e.g. 'the major's own count').
The last line calls back to the hook or loops into it, so a replay feels intentional.
Use 'gap' (seconds of silence after a line) for comic timing: 0.4-0.6 s before a punchline.
Every drawn number has its source and year written small beside it on the page.

radar: Science news this month that makes a hypothetical timely (missions, discoveries, records)
Questions people ask (Reddit r/askscience, r/NoStupidQuestions, xkcd What If archive for style, never to copy)
Our YouTube API scans: 'what would happen if' and science-animation outliers
avoid: Partisan framing: explain mechanisms, name sources, no villains
Stories without an official or primary source

preferred: Peer-reviewed papers and university press releases
Textbook physics with the calculation shown in the dossier
sources.notes: Datasets are downloaded into the episode folder with the source URL and access date.

publishing.cadence: pilot: one video, then decide with the user

open_decisions: Channel name and handle (working name 'Drawn Out'): the user's call
The hand: photoreal cut-out from a Nano Banana image (prompt in the chat log, 2026-10-07); a still frame first
